method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill, from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Income Tax Rates Act 1986, Compilation No. 66, compilation date 1 July 2026, includes amendments up to Act No. 50, 2026 (Register id C2026C00300), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03348.txt; the rates are in the Act's own text (no other instrument sets them)
license: Apache-2.0 for the L4; the quoted statutory text is reproduced under CC BY 4.0 with the attribution in ../../SOURCE-LICENSE.md

checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read.

scope: From the seat of the taxpayer: s 3 (tax-free threshold of $18,200, prescribed non-resident, resident taxpayer, ordinary taxable income, non-profit company), s 3A (working holiday makers), s 12(1), Schedule 7 Parts I-III with clause 4 (resident tables for 2024-25/2025-26 at 16%, 2026-27 at 15%, 2027-28 and later at 14%, then 30/37/45%; one non-resident and one working holiday maker table from 2024-25), ss 16, 18, 20(1) (part-year residency; the pro-rated threshold is an input because the deposit drops the formula), ss 23(2), 23(6), 23AA, 23AB (company rate 25% for a base rate entity, else 30%; non-profit ceiling). Years before 2024-25 and abnormal-income averaging return 'Not in the deposited text'. Not encoded: Schedule 7 clauses 2-3, ss 12(2)-(13), 12AA, 12A, 13-15, 20(1A)-(3), Schedules 8-12, s 23(3)-(5), (7), 23A, 25-30, rounding.
seat: the taxpayer (an individual; and, in Daniel's life, the founder asking at what rate his company is taxed)
